name: pick-the-path
query: I want to put GitHub's public MCP server (https://mcp.github.com/mcp) and our internal Notion MCP server behind Cloudflare with Google SSO for my team. We don't have Cloudflare in Terraform today. What's the fastest way? Should I write a Terraform module?
expected_behavior: Recommends Path A (AI Controls MCP Portal via REST) for this case — multiple existing MCP URLs, want one URL fronting them with OAuth, no existing IaC. Calls out that Terraform (Path C) is overkill here because there's no Cloudflare IaC to extend.

Lists the actual steps for Path A: create the Google IdP via REST, POST each server to /accounts/{aid}/access/ai-controls/mcp/servers with auth_type=oauth, complete the dashboard OAuth handshake for each server, create the Access policy with `require { login_method }`, then assemble the portal in the dashboard.

Acknowledges that the internal Notion MCP needs to be publicly reachable (or sit behind its own tunnel) for the portal to reach it — Path A doesn't tunnel for you; if Notion MCP is private-only, suggest a small Path B carve-out (Access app + tunnel for that one server) and point the portal at the resulting public hostname.
Flags the AI Controls limit: auth_type is oauth/bearer/unauthenticated only — no Cloudflare Access service-token (dual-header) auth to the upstream.
Mentions that portal URL composition is currently dashboard-driven (not fully REST). Plan for that manual step.
Does NOT recommend Terraform as the default just because the user said 'module'.
Does NOT silently default to Path B (per-hostname Access apps) when the user has 2 URLs and is happy with a portal.
